name: 07-drivers-desktop
description: What carries the frame out of the device, on a desktop: a preview, the video senders, and the network protocols a fixture listens on.

steps.title: Drivers
steps.description: Getting the frame out, on a desktop
steps.caption: Drivers. Getting the finished frame out of the device.
A driver carries the finished frame out of the device. One frame, and as many drivers as you like carrying it at once.
This is a computer, so the ones worth showing here are the ones that send the frame somewhere rather than clocking it onto a pin.
Preview draws the frame in your browser, which is what you have been watching in every one of these clips.
N D I sends the frame onto the network as video, so O B S or Resolume can pick it up as a source like any camera.
Taking it out again. A driver is a module like any other, so adding and removing one is the same gesture throughout.
R T S P serves the same frame as a stream, which a player opens by U R L over the network.
Out it goes. Several of these can run at once, each driving its own slice of the same buffer.
H L S writes the frame out as segments any player opens, V L C on a laptop or on the television.
And away. Notice the lights never stop while I do this: a driver comes and goes on the next frame.

Network send speaks Art Net, s A C N and D D P, so real fixtures on a real rig listen to this one. Moving heads and par cans take the same universes a strip does: a fixture is lights and a few channels of pan, tilt and color, which is a layout like any other.
Removing it again, because the next one goes lower than I P.
Panel card talks to the receiving cards a professional rig is built from, over raw Ethernet frames below I P, the way a sender card does.
And out, because the last one is the most domestic of the set.
Hue drives the bulbs in the room through their own bridge, so the same effect lands on the lamps you already own.
And that one goes too, leaving the device the way we found it.
One frame, and any of these carries it. The pin drivers are in this same list, and they come into their own on a device that has pins to clock.
